title: FAITHFUL ASTRALITE baby: Picta keeps its body and brightness; Astralite's authored dawn/day/dusk colour moves into the records (Route A); E11 filters become luma-locked grey scalars; Astralite's coloured volumetric air, mist rings, MoT mist banks and misty-weather density are transplanted
pitch: In game the baby is Picta everywhere that is not a dawn, day or dusk colour. That covers the cloud panoramas and dome shape, the night (identical on screen), interiors, water, SH2/KiSuite grade, CLMT timing, seasons, summer weathers and every brightness key. From about 06:30 to 20:00 the colours are Astralite's as authored. The zenith goes indigo, then royal blue. The horizon turns coral/salmon at dawn and dusk, both toward and away from the sun: modelled dome hue toward the sun is 259-263 deg in Picta, 6 deg in the baby and 7 deg in Astralite. Far fog turns coral and clouds turn coral at dusk. Sun-side ambient goes rose-mauve (338 deg) with plum shadows (302 deg), matching Astralite to the degree. Day ambient is periwinkle and noon light is pinkish-beige; day clouds are white. Cloudy, fog, rain and snow weathers take Astralite's own cooler and greyer palettes. On top of that come peach, rose and gold volumetric air at dawn and dusk, soft grey day air, distant mist rings, Mists of Tamriel banks tinted rose at dawn, and denser misty weathers. Why this route: Bottled E11 multiplies record colour by filter (ColorFilter(c,F,0)=c*F). Picta's hue lives in strongly blue filters, so Astralite records dropped under them double-tint. The naive model gives a dawn horizon of 283-322 deg instead of 7, at 0.58-0.97x luma, and near fog at 21-26x luma. The faithful fix does what Astralite does: hue goes in the records, and Picta's filters become grey scalars. Those scalars are solved by least squares so that Rec.709 on-screen luma matches Picta every 15 minutes from 05:00 to 21:00. Sky, clouds, fog and ambient stay within 4.7%. Night output stays exact, because Night records are scaled x m and Night filters / m. The only strength dial is Astralite chroma amplitude, using the house c' = L + (c-L)*k transform, which keeps hue and luma locked. An earlier 85/15 Picta/Astralite hue mix was rejected: it produced magenta and grey intermediates wherever the two hues oppose.

title: PICTA-SAFE baby: Picta with Astralite tones mixed into its own Effects 11 filters at locked brightness, plus additive Astralite mists
pitch:
In game the baby still looks like Picta. Every brightness, exposure, intensity, fog-distance and contrast value is unchanged, and so are the night, the interiors, the seasons and the summer weathers. What changes is the colour inside that brightness. At dawn and dusk (around 07:15 and 18:45) Picta's cold blue twilight horizon turns lavender-violet. The sky near the sun turns rose-pink, the distant fog turns mauve, clouds pick up violet, and ambient light and Picta's own mountain fog banks warm toward Astralite's rose-mauve. At midday Picta's very saturated blues soften toward Astralite's royal-blue and periwinkle palette (horizon saturation 0.84 to 0.68), and sunlight turns slightly pinker. Rain, fog and snow weathers go a little greyer, as Astralite's do. Astralite's mists are added on top: its faint distant fog rings (Lite on clear and cloudy weathers, Heavy on misty and foggy ones, Rain on rain and snow) and Mists of Tamriel's animated distant mist banks on cloudy, foggy and aurora weathers. Astralite's re-skin of MoT's ground mists is included too and shows once the MoT volumetric-mist toggle is on.

Why this design: the map shows that Picta's records are grey and all of its hue lives in its per-weather E11 filters. Dropping Astralite records under those filters multiplies the two and gives a muddy blue-violet sunset (257 deg). So records stay grey and the hue is moved inside Picta's own filters with an exact luminance lock. That is solved over every 15-minute step of the day through the real Bottled 4ca678b chain, not just at the period peaks. Records are touched only where E11 has no lever: ambient (DALC) and sky-statics colour. Every piece lives in four new baby-only mods and one ESL, so turning them off gives Picta back byte-for-byte. One master dial (STRENGTH, default 0.6) sets how much Astralite is mixed in. That dial is an amplitude, which fits the user's "too strong = amplitude only" rule.

title: Picta x Astralite "baby": per-channel physics design (one hue carrier per channel, kept on Picta's clocks, OKLCh mix with locked brightness)
pitch: At noon and at night the baby looks like Picta: it has the same brightness, the same blue zenith and the same moonlight. Interiors, seasons, summer weathers, the fair climate and the Helios exits behave exactly as in Picta. The difference is in the dawn and dusk windows (Picta's own 06:00-09:00 and 17:00-20:00). The violet-blue horizon swings through mauve toward rose-coral (A01 dawn horizon hue 280°->319°, C01 280°->343°). Clouds and far fog pick up the same rose-coral cast. The low sun gives a softer, warmer orange light (chroma 0.165->0.141). Ambient light turns rose on the sun side and plum on the shade side. By day the sky shifts slightly toward Astralite's royal blue. Rain and fog weathers keep their hue but lose 30-45% of Picta's blue, because Astralite's partners for them are neutral grey. On top of that, Astralite's air is added. There is peach or gold volumetric glow at dawn and dusk, a light grey density haze by day, and dense grey fog volume in rain and fog. Astralite's camera-ring distant mists appear, as do the Mists of Tamriel animated valley mists that Astralite enables. The volumetric light is never weaker than Picta's own god rays. Why it is built this way: every colour channel is a product of record and ini factors on two clocks (records follow CLMT, ini values follow TIMEOFDAY). So each channel gets exactly one lever, which carries a correction toward a blended target. That lever is the one that already carries Picta's hue on the same clock. The blend is done in OKLCh at equal luminance and then locked to Picta's luminance. With every mix set to 0, the design reproduces Picta exactly in all five modelled weathers. The rejected alternatives broke this by 20-38% in light brightness. On the volumetric-light question: fVolumetricLightingIntensity=0.0 in the Darkened plugin ini does not kill VOLI. The same ini sets bVolumetricLightingUpdateWeather=1. Bottled's VL feature also forces VL on in exteriors and multiplies the per-frame, weather-rewritten render data in place. So the baby ships that ini unchanged and gates the volumetric-fog piece behind a quick in-game probe. If the probe fails, that piece does nothing.
